correctness.rationale: Every fixed point has common opinion y=p+q ubar. The dissatisfied and adopter fixed-point equations then force a common adopter fraction when ubar>0, or u=0 everywhere, excluding heterogeneous equilibria. With p=0 and a>0 the sole positive-adopter equation beta q^2 a^2(H-a)=delta on (0,H) has exactly 0/1/2 solutions by the maximum 4H^3/27 at a=2H/3. At beta=4/9, delta=1/128, g=1/8, alpha=3/8, lambda=1/4, xi=3/8, independent Fraction recomputation finds q=1/2,H=7/8,beta_c=108/343, equilibria (a,v,y)=(0,1,0),(3/8,17/32,3/16),(3/4,13/64,3/8). The full Jacobian decomposes into one 3x3 consensus block and n-1 transverse (2x2+0) blocks; independent roots show E- has exactly one multiplier >1 and all others <1, E0 and E+ are sinks. Hyperbolic persistence and simple nonzero fixed-point roots establish the stated small positive baseline continuation.
residual_risks: The zero-predisposition threshold is not generalized to heterogeneous matrices or all positive baseline p; persistence only for sufficiently small r and the specific hyperbolic example.

final_claim: For homogeneous complete-mixing SAD/Friedkin–Johnsen adoption dynamics the zero-baseline positive-equilibrium fold occurs at beta_c=27 delta/(4q^2H^3) for H>0, with exact 0/1/2 positive roots; a rational admissible parameter instance has two hyperbolic sinks separated by a saddle in full 3n dimensions and persists for sufficiently small positive predisposition.
limitations: The zero-predisposition threshold is not generalized to heterogeneous matrices or all positive baseline p; persistence only for sufficiently small r and the specific hyperbolic example.
